items.title: Finite Markov decision process with joint reward-transition law
items.statement: A finite MDP has a finite state set S (possibly empty), a finite reward alphabet R contained in the real numbers, a finite nonempty action set A(s) for each s in S, and a joint probability mass p(s′,ρ|s,a) on S×R for each admissible pair (s,a). Put r(s,a)=Σ_{s′,ρ}ρp(s′,ρ|s,a) and P(s′|s,a)=Σ_ρp(s′,ρ|s,a). A stationary Markov policy is a family π(a|s) of probability distributions on A(s); a deterministic policy selects one action in each A(s).
items.strategy: Specify the finite one-step joint reward-transition model and its policy conventions; define the expected reward and state-transition law by finite sums.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown University Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: Absolute convergence and tail bound for bounded discounted rewards
items.statement: Let M≥0, 0≤γ<1, and let (ρj)j≥1 be any real sequence with |ρj|≤M. The series G=Σj≥0 γjρj+1 converges absolutely. Every partial sum and its limit have absolute value at most M/(1−γ), and for every N≥0, |G−Σj<N γjρj+1|≤MγN/(1−γ), with the empty partial sum at N=0.
items.strategy: Compare the absolute reward terms with the geometric series, then pass the finite geometric tail bound to the limit.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Completeness of the sup metric on finite-state value functions
items.statement: For any finite set S, let B(S)=R^S. If S is empty, set d∞(u,v)=0; otherwise set d∞(u,v)=maxs∈S|u(s)−v(s)|. Then d∞ is a metric on B(S), and (B(S),d∞) is complete.
items.strategy: Identify a nonempty finite state set with n for n≥1, compare the max metric and Euclidean metric, and transfer completeness from R^n; treat the empty set separately.

references.title: Sergey Mozgovoy, Lecture Notes on Metric Spaces and Functional Analysis

items.title: A finite MDP and stationary policy generate a reward-state Markov chain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite MDP with nonempty state set S and a stationary Markov policy π, put E=S×(R∪{0}) and Kπ((s,ρ),B)=Σaπ(a|s)Σ(s′,ρ′)∈S×R 1B(s′,ρ′)p(s′,ρ′|s,a). Then Kπ is a probability kernel on E. For every s∈S there is a probability law on EN whose coordinate process starts at (s,0) and is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel Kπ relative to its natural filtration.
items.strategy: Check that the finite mixture defines a probability kernel, then apply the published Ionescu–Tulcea construction and the library chain definition.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown University Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: Policy Bellman operator
items.statement: For a finite MDP, discount 0≤γ<1, and stationary Markov policy π, the policy Bellman operator Tπ:R^S→R^S is (TπV)(s)=Σa∈A(s)π(a|s)[r(s,a)+γΣs′∈S P(s′|s,a)V(s′)].
items.strategy: Define the one-step policy evaluation map from the joint reward-transition law and the stationary policy.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown University Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: Bellman optimality operator
items.statement: For a finite MDP and discount 0≤γ<1, the Bellman optimality operator T*:R^S→R^S is (T*V)(s)=maxa∈A(s)[r(s,a)+γΣs′∈S P(s′|s,a)V(s′)].
items.strategy: Define the one-step optimality map using a maximum over each finite nonempty action set.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown University Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: Discounted returns and policy values in a finite MDP
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite MDP, stationary Markov policy π, and 0≤γ<1, under the canonical reward-state chain started from X0=(s,0), write Xt=(St,Rt) and define Gt=Σj≥0γjRt+j+1 and Vπ(s)=Eπ,s[G0]. The series is measurable, integrable, and bounded in absolute value by M/(1−γ). If S is empty, Vπ is the unique empty function. This is the start-state meaning of Eπ[Gt|St=s] when that conditional expectation is defined. Average-reward and undiscounted continuing models, and improper episodic tasks, are outside this definition.
items.strategy: Define the discounted return under the actual policy-induced path law; use the finite reward bound and geometric tail estimate for well-definedness.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown University Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: Finite-MDP Bellman operators are gamma contractions with unique fixed points
items.statement: Let a finite MDP and 0≤γ<1 be fixed. For every stationary policy π and all V,W∈R^S, ‖TπV−TπW‖∞≤γ‖V−W‖∞; likewise ‖T*V−T*W‖∞≤γ‖V−W‖∞. Each operator has exactly one fixed point. The contraction constant is the nonnegative number γ.
items.strategy: Bound the finite probability-weighted averages and finite maxima in sup norm, then apply Banach with q=γ on the complete finite-state value space.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown University Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: Exact value iteration for the Bellman optimality operator
items.statement: Input a finite MDP, 0≤γ<1, an initial value V0∈R^S, and an integer m≥0. Set Vj+1=T*Vj for j=0,…,m−1 and return Vm. The procedure returns the exact mth iterate and makes no finite-termination claim for convergence.
items.strategy: Specify the exact finite number of Bellman optimality backups and the returned iterate.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Expected discounted policy value is a fixed point of its Bellman operator
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite MDP, 0≤γ<1, and stationary Markov policy π, the expected discounted value Vπ defined from each initial state satisfies TπVπ=Vπ.
items.strategy: Derive the finite-horizon first-step recursion from the induced chain’s finite-prefix law, then pass to the bounded discounted-return limit.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown University Technical Report CS-96-08

items.title: Value iteration converges at the Bellman contraction rate
items.statement: Let V* be the unique fixed point of T*. For every initial V0∈R^S and every m≥0, the iterates Vm=T*Vm−1 from exact value iteration satisfy ‖Vm−V*‖∞≤γm‖V0−V*‖∞, with γ0=1.
items.strategy: Apply the contraction inequality repeatedly, with equality at the initial index.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Exact finite policy iteration with retained greedy actions
items.statement: Input a finite MDP, 0≤γ<1, an initial deterministic policy π0, and for each s an ordered list containing every member of A(s) exactly once. At iteration k, compute the unique exact fixed point Vk=TπkVk. For each s, let Qk(s,a)=r(s,a)+γΣs′P(s′|s,a)Vk(s′); retain πk(s) if it attains maxa Qk(s,a), and otherwise choose the earliest maximizing action in the supplied list. If πk+1=πk, return (πk,Vk); otherwise repeat.
items.strategy: Define exact policy evaluation, deterministic greedy improvement using a supplied action list, tie retention, and the stop condition.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Greedy policy improvement and finite policy-iteration termination
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let a finite MDP have 0≤γ<1, and let π be any stationary Markov policy with expected discounted value Vπ. Any deterministic policy π′ greedy with respect to Vπ satisfies Vπ′(s)≥Vπ(s) for every s; if Tπ′Vπ(s)>Vπ(s) at some state, the inequality is strict at some state. Exact finite policy iteration with the stated tie-retention rule strictly improves at every changed policy, makes at most Πs∈S|A(s)|−1 changes, and terminates at a deterministic policy with value V* that dominates every stationary policy.
items.strategy: Use the Bellman fixed-point identities, monotonicity of positive probability averages, contraction iteration, and finiteness of deterministic policies; retain the current action at every tie.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

title: Finite MDPs and Bellman operators — Examples

items.title: A unit reward on a self-loop has no finite undiscounted return
items.statement: Take S={s}, A(s)={a}, R={1}, and p(s,1|s,a)=1. At γ=1 the return partial sum through N−1 is N, so the infinite undiscounted return diverges; the formal one-state Bellman update F(v)=1+v has no fixed point and is not a contraction with any q<1.
items.strategy: Compute the finite partial sums and solve the formal fixed-point equation directly.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: A common reward shift moves every one-state Bellman value equally
items.statement: Let S={s}, A(s)={a,b}, γ=1/2, and let both actions return to s with probability one and have deterministic rewards 1 and 3, respectively. The unique fixed points of their policy Bellman operators are 2 and 6. Adding 2 to both rewards changes the fixed points to 6 and 10, so both move by 2/(1−γ)=4, their difference remains 4, and b remains greedy for the Bellman optimality operator.
items.strategy: Evaluate the two geometric discounted returns before and after the common reward shift.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: A one-state value-iteration model attains the Bellman error bound
items.statement: Let S={s}, A(s)={a}, γ=1/2, with a deterministic self-loop reward 1, and initialize V0(s)=0. Then V*=2 and Vm(s)=2(1−2^(−m)), so ‖Vm−V*‖∞=2^(1−m)=γ^m‖V0−V*‖∞ for every m≥0.
items.strategy: Solve the scalar Bellman fixed point and prove the iterate formula by induction.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Changing a tied greedy action can cycle, while retention stops
items.statement: Let S={s}, A(s)={a,b}, γ=1/2, and let both actions give reward 0 and return deterministically to s. Both actions are greedy for every value. Exact policy iteration retains the current action and stops after one evaluation; a rule that always switches to a different maximizing action alternates forever between a and b.
items.strategy: Compute the unique policy value, verify both actions tie, and compare the retained rule with the specified switching rule.

references.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.
